gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Noto Sans Tirhuta reads crisp and open, with a dominant x-height. Neon's glowing, pencil-line strokes sit above it, so the sans-serif text feels like a quiet answer to a bright sign.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Noto Sans Ugaritic has a very short step from lowercase to capital, and its open letter mouths feel like chalk arcs left unjoined. Neon brings stencil-cut letters of one steady width, and that glow keeps the soft text from drifting.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-vai: Neon sets glowing, stamped-metal lowercase with joints that never thin or bulge where strokes meet. Noto Sans Vai follows with generous space between curve ends and stems, so its words settle into solid blocks.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Vibrant is the first word for Neon, whose thickness stays put around every curve. Noto Sans Vithkuqi counters that with open throats and a minimal step up to capitals, a modern, clean companion.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Noto Sans Wancho reads hulking and chalky, its lowercase pressed hard and its e wide open at the terminal. Neon is the sharper side of the pair, a glowing heading whose t has a crossbar and stem sharing one width.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-warang-citi: Glowing monoline up top, solid blocks below. Neon runs one line width from stem to serif, while Noto Sans Warang Citi lets wide channels lead into each counter so the sans text stays easy on the eye.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-s: Approachable describes Noto Sans Zanabazar Square, with its soaring x-height and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. And Neon's strokes, free of thin and thick, give that soft body a glowing, stamped-metal partner.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-traditional-nush: Noto Traditional Nushu moves like a broad-nibbed pen that never curls shut, with bowls filling the line. Neon, pipe-bodied in every stroke, glows above it.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-numans: Numans spreads out with swollen, rope-tight lowercase, tracking pushed far and an s whose ends hang from the spine. Neon, flat and unmodulated, glows over it.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-onest: Onest reads friendly and contemporary, with short ascenders above big bowls and no ink pooling where curves turn in. Onest keeps a gentle monotone line across a full page, so Neon's glowing heading never has to compete with it.
